product_contract.request_protection: A workspace termination refresh extends the active terminate-request interruption deadline so late system interruptions cannot close the panel.
product_contract.termination_authority: Confirmed process termination is recorded by the repair provider before provider evidence is committed, preventing a lagging directory snapshot from republishing the dead PID.
product_contract.projection_ownership: Degraded committed projections retain their protected cross-consumer semantics while the active Switcher filters the confirmed terminated process from its session payload.
product_contract.process_identity: A different running PID with the same bundle-derived app identity survives termination filtering.
product_contract.window_cycle_continuity: An active window cycle retains its prior window order, selection, and runtime context when the same process temporarily publishes zero windows during repair.
product_contract.visible_workflow: Control-Tab and Option-Tab continue to open, navigate, and commit through Mock and real topology; a selected real fixture remains visible until workspace termination evidence arrives and is then removed without collapsing the session.

production_path: SwitcherPanelController converts a confirmed workspace termination into an extended interruption-protection interval before refreshing the session.
RuntimeProjectionService records the terminated PID in the repair provider, commits provider evidence, then marks and commits the main-table app-switcher projection.
LiveSwitcherModel refreshes the active projection with the confirmed app and PID identity, filters only that process at the Switcher boundary, and preserves any surviving different PID.
LiveSwitcherModel restores an active window cycle from its last complete same-process app and context when a degraded refresh temporarily carries zero windows.
Existing Mock and real-fixture UI workflows exercise the ordinary panel, pointer, keyboard, Spaces, AX/CG, and process-lifecycle paths.

test_meaning_conclusion.classification: retain existing tests unchanged and add four independent lifecycle regressions
test_meaning_conclusion.protected_meaning: A quit request is intent; workspace termination and provider evidence establish process death, degraded projections remain valid for their existing consumers, and only the active Switcher applies immediate confirmed-process filtering.
independent_oracle: Termination refresh cannot shorten a previously established request-protection deadline.
A provider snapshot containing a terminated PID cannot republish that PID after signalAppTerminated returns.
A same-process degraded projection with zero windows cannot erase the visible window-cycle order or selection.
A degraded committed projection may retain a terminated app while the active Switcher session removes the confirmed PID.
Existing same-bundle different-PID and read-model dirty-generation contracts remain unchanged.
Visible Mock and real workflows prove panel trigger, selection, commit, fullscreen/off-Space continuity, and process-lifetime removal.

test_quality_conclusion.flake_assessment: The final candidate passed fourteen app-host tests, seven Mock UI tests, two real trigger/topology tests, and one isolated real quit test.
test_quality_conclusion.target_reachability: The canonical FlowTabTests and UI wrappers compiled the production and new test source through the FlowTab target.

prechange_request_deadline_behavior.signal: Workspace termination refresh replaced the longer request-protection deadline with a shorter refresh deadline.

prechange_provider_order_behavior.signal: The terminated PID remained in both app-directory and app-switcher projections after a lagging provider snapshot was committed.

prechange_window_cycle_behavior.signal: A degraded refresh erased the active window list, selected window, and runtime window context.

prechange_degraded_termination_behavior.signal: A degraded committed projection reintroduced the confirmed terminated app into the active Switcher session.

prechange_real_quit_ui.signal: The visible Switcher summary became empty during the real fixture quit lifecycle.

root_cause.request_deadline: The termination refresh used replacement semantics and shortened an already longer request-protection deadline.
root_cause.provider_commit_order: RuntimeProjectionService committed the app-directory provider snapshot before recording the terminated PID in the provider, allowing stale evidence to win the same maintenance turn.
root_cause.window_cycle_refresh: Projection refresh rebuilt the selected same-process app from a temporarily empty window payload and discarded the active window-cycle state before repair completed.
root_cause.consumer_boundary: The active Switcher reloaded a deliberately stale committed projection after termination and had no event-scoped PID filter, while changing the shared read model would violate protected degraded-projection semantics.

semantic_delta.request_protection: Termination refresh extends the current deadline instead of replacing it.
semantic_delta.provider_order: The repair provider records process termination before its evidence is committed and main-table projection work is marked dirty.
semantic_delta.window_cycle: The active same-process window cycle restores the previous complete app windows, selection order, and runtime context across a zero-window degraded refresh.
semantic_delta.termination_filter: The confirmed app and PID flow into the app-switcher loader, which removes that process only from the active Switcher payload when no surviving different PID is known.
semantic_delta.shared_projection_semantics: RuntimeReadModelStore behavior and existing degraded committed projections remain unchanged.
semantic_delta.tests: Four additive behavior regressions cover deadline, provider ordering, degraded window continuity, and consumer-boundary termination filtering.
